statements.t: We are currently targeting the battery electric vehicle market due to the size and perceived demand for next generation battery technology but believe our technologies can also have broader applications in robotics, defense and aviation, and off-highway markets, as these markets mature.
To satisfy anticipated demand, we will need to scale production of our electrolyte.
Since many factors are difficult to quantify, our actual operating results may be different than currently anticipated.
We will need to continue to deploy substantial capital to expand our production capabilities and engage in research and development programs.
We also expect to continue to incur administrative expenses as a publicly traded company.

For the remainder of 2026, we expect revenue recognition to continue to decrease relative to prior year periods as we focus on our site acceptance testing, commissioning and operational startup of the continuous electrolyte production pilot line ( MOBIUS™) and provide electrolyte to our partners and customers.

We anticipate that our most significant capital expenditures for the remainder of the year will relate to construction of our continuous electrolyte production pilot line ( MOBIUS™ ) as well as improvements to our cell development capabilities.

If financing is not available, or if the terms of financing are less desirable than we expect, we may be forced to take actions to reduce our capital or operating expenditures, which may adversely affect our development, business, operating results, financial condition and prospects.

We expect cash used in operating activities for the remainder of the year to increase on a quarterly basis as we continue to achieve our development objectives and focus on driving electrolyte product competitiveness and commercialization.

Cash used for capital expenditures and intangibles increased $6.4 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 due to timing of milestone payments on our capital projects.
“We also advanced discussions regarding a potential joint venture in the Republic of Korea as we plan to establish commercial-scale electrolyte manufacturing capabilities.
While EVs will continue to be our north star as we scale up, we are also actively pursuing new markets for our technology.
Management has reduced its expected 2026 cash investment guidance to be in the range of $75 million to $85 million compared to its prior range of $85 million to $100 million.
The revised outlook reflects our continued focus on driving innovation, building internal capabilities and supporting our partners and customers while optimizing expenses.

Solid Power’s business model – selling its electrolyte to cell manufacturers and licensing its cell designs and manufacturing processes – distinguishes the company from many of its competitors who plan to be commercial battery manufacturers.

These statements may include, but are not limited to, statements regarding potential new joint ventures and anticipated collaboration agreements, Solid Power’s technology, strategy, business model, market opportunity, operations, future prospects, and plans and objectives of management.
